reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the transition from shear banding to kinking-like deformation and strain delocalization at ~10 nm layer thickness in a CuTiZrNb high-entropy alloy nanolayered glass. However, it does not address time-dependent plastic deformation (creep) or sustained loading, leaving the final premise unsupported.
premises: Reducing layer thickness to ~10 nm increases density of amorphous-like interfaces
Increased interface density shifts deformation from shear banding to kinking-like mechanism
Transition to kinking-like deformation delocalizes strain
Strain delocalization suppresses time-dependent plastic deformation
